newsitem.title: USA: New ADRs totaled $4.1 bln in Q3 - Bankers Trust.
newsitem.headline: New ADRs totaled $4.1 bln in Q3 - Bankers Trust.

text.p: New American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) raised a total of $4.1 billion in the third quarter of 1996, a sharp rise from the same period last year, Bankers Trust Co said on Tuesday.
The company said in a statement 49 new ADR programs were established in the quarter ended Sept 30.
"These numbers show an increase from third quarter 1995 figures, where only 32 new programs were established and $1.3 billion was raised using Depositary Receipts," it said.
ADRs allow Americans to buy shares of foreign-based companies in the United States, and the ADRS -- also known as American Depositary Shares -- are traded on U.S. exchanges.

In the first nine months of 1996, total capital raised through ADR programs totaled $10.3 billion, an increase of 87 percent from the same period last year, when $5.5 billion was raised. Through September this year, a total of 151 new ADR programs from 46 countries were establish, compared with 105 from 31 countries in the same period in 1995.
The increase is seen as arising from a renewal of ADR deals in Latin America and from new ADR activity from Eastern Europe and Asia.
